rationale: Test the new read-support consumption obligation with a real committed joint transition, delayed producer replies and an independent quorum ledger.

feedback.answered: The discriminator now has a complete producer-derived harness: initial five voters, one pending unique read, an actual committed explicit-joint reduction, and delayed heartbeat responses released in fixed order. The expected incoming/outgoing sets come from inputs and are checked against actual ConfState; the oracle does not use readOnly.acks.
remaining: Trusted-runner execution and review must establish the actual read-output timing, support counts and control completion.
Client read endpoints and multi-request batching remain independent limits.
feedback.rationale: Old-only support after joint application distinguishes stale request-time eligibility from current joint qualification; response 4 supplies a permitted completion control.

candidate.rationale: Fix a necessary local eligibility condition from documented safe-read quorum and joint-majority semantics; do not equate this condition with full client linearizability.

question.question: For one unique outstanding ReadOnlySafe request retained while an explicit joint configuration is applied, can acknowledgments forming only an outgoing majority release a ReadState before an incoming majority also supports that context?
question.importance: If removed voters alone can authorize a read after the joint configuration is active, the library could hand out read authority without the configured overlap protection. The immediate duty is qualified ReadState release; client-visible stale reads require additional history and application observations not supplied by this question.
participants: Leader, outgoing voters and retained incoming voters
Application applying a committed explicit-joint configuration entry
contexts: ReadOnlySafe; unique nonempty request context used once
Leader has committed a current-term entry before request
Explicit joint transition removes two voters from an initial five-voter configuration; leader remains a voter
No role or term change between request and observed release

counterevidence: The heartbeat consumer explicitly invokes current r.trk.Voters.VoteResult, whose JointConfig implementation requires both majority configurations.
switchToConfig does not clear the pending acknowledgment set, so preservation does not itself imply a defect.
A later context can release earlier queued requests; restricting this question to a single request is necessary to avoid an unsupported per-request majority assertion.
question.trigger_rationale: The current-configuration consumer and retained context-keyed support give a concrete distinction between an old-only majority and both joint majorities. Five initial voters transitioning to incoming {1,4,5} and outgoing {1,2,3,4,5} permits actual delayed replies from 2 and 3 to form only the outgoing majority with leader 1; reply 4 then supplies the incoming majority. This avoids fabricated membership state and needs no new process or snapshot bootstrap.

obligation.description: For a single outstanding ReadOnlySafe request consumed while an explicit joint voter configuration is active, release of its ReadState requires acknowledgment support satisfying both incoming and outgoing voter majorities. Support from only the outgoing majority must not authorize release.

scope.description: One unique outstanding ReadOnlySafe context across application of an explicit joint change from five voters to incoming {1,4,5}, outgoing {1,2,3,4,5}, with leader 1 retained in the same term.
assumptions: Actual RawNode-generated heartbeat responses, held and later delivered unchanged.
Current-term leader entry committed/applied before ReadIndex; joint change proposed, replicated, committed and applied through public APIs.
Exactly one ReadIndex invocation with a fresh nonempty context; no retries or later requests can release a queue prefix.
Single-threaded RawNode calls, reliable FIFO asynchronous storage handling, MemoryStorage as a no-crash completion adapter.
No ticks, role changes, term changes, further configuration changes or client read service during the observed suffix.
excluded: Multiple read request batching, reused request contexts, lease-based reads and singleton fast paths.
Physical storage durability and crash/restart behavior.
General liveness; absence of release is permitted until qualified support.

grounding.derivation: S_options assigns ReadOnlySafe quorum communication to read authority. JointConfig documents decisions requiring both majority sets; S_leader_other explicitly applies that voter rule before advancing read requests. With one outstanding request, no later context can supply batched confirmation. The local necessary condition is therefore ReadState release implies support satisfying both active sets. This does not assert that the condition alone proves client-visible linearizability, nor that an unqualified request must complete.
grounding.applicability: Same leader and request context span an actual applied explicit-joint transition. The incoming and outgoing sets are independently fixed by the driver inputs and checked against returned implementation ConfState.
alternatives: Stored acknowledgments need not be discarded on configuration change; current-set qualification may be sufficient for this local responsibility.
ReadState index may remain the original pre-configuration commit index; the contract does not require equality with the latest commit.

associations.rationale: This is the read support consumer; configuration application updates the voter sets it consults without replacing the pending request object.

bindings.description: Checks current voter JointConfig against context-keyed acknowledgments before advancing pending ReadIndex statuses and constructing ReadState output.
